title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). G is a group, 𝔊 ⊂ G is a normal subgroup with quotient γ = G/𝔊, and (φ_i : N_i → G)_{i∈I} is a family of homomorphisms. Put SN_i = φ_i^{-1}(𝔊). Condition (12) requires each composite N_i → γ to be surjective. The aim is to rebuild G from 𝔊 together with the local data (N_i, SN_i, φ_i|SN_i : SN_i → 𝔊, θ_i : N_i → Aut(𝔊)). This is a kind of relative amalgamated sum.

Step 1: one index at a time (diagram (15)). For fixed i, the data are:
- an extension SN_i ⊂ N_i with quotient γ_i = N_i/SN_i;
- a homomorphism φ_i : SN_i → 𝔊;
- an action θ_i of N_i on 𝔊.
These are subject to conditions (3)a,b, presumably:
- θ_i restricted to SN_i equals Int∘φ_i;
- φ_i is N_i-equivariant.
From these one forms the pushout extension
G_i = (𝔊 ⋊_{θ_i} N_i) / {(φ_i(s)^{-1}, s) : s ∈ SN_i}.
G_i is an extension of γ_i by 𝔊 and fits in the square SN_i → 𝔊, SN_i ⊂ N_i → G_i ⊃ 𝔊. By surjectivity (12), G = 𝔊·φ_i(N_i), and the universal property gives a canonical isomorphism G_i ≅ G that is the identity on 𝔊. So each single index already recovers G as an abstract extension.

Step 2: gluing the indices. Grothendieck observes that the full situation (11) is recovered once one gives a transitive system of isomorphisms between the G_i that induce the identity on 𝔊.
- Such a system induces a transitive system of isomorphisms between the γ_i = N_i/SN_i, so they can be identified with one group γ, the common quotient (16)–(17).
- Identifying each G_i/𝔊 with γ (18), he forms the fibre product 𝒢 = ∏_{γ} G_i over γ. This is an extension of γ by 𝔊^I (next page, (19)).
- The gluing data then correspond to subgroups G ⊂ 𝒢 with G ∩ 𝔊^I = the diagonal δ(𝔊), and with G → γ surjective (20). Equivalently, they correspond to restricting the extension 𝒢 to an extension of γ by the diagonal 𝔊.

The page sits in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' material. It plausibly serves to describe a profinite group (e.g. a fundamental group or a Galois–Teichmüller-type group) by local pieces such as normalisers of inertia or decomposition subgroups. These are glued along a common normal subgroup 𝔊 (e.g. a geometric fundamental group) over a common quotient γ.
errors: Normality of 𝔊 in G is implicit; it is needed for γ = G/𝔊 to be a group.

Redundancy: a transitive system of isomorphisms G_i ≅ G_j that is the identity on 𝔊 already determines the identifications of the γ_i, so the 'compatibility with the γ-system' on the next page is automatic.

Correctness check of (20): for G ⊂ 𝒢 with G ∩ 𝔊^I = diagonal and G ↠ γ, each projection p_i : G → G_i is injective (kernel ⊂ diagonal ∩ ker p_i = 1) and surjective (its image contains 𝔊 and maps onto γ). So the equivalence with transitive isomorphism systems holds. No genuine error.
When 𝔊 has nontrivial centre, the choice of isomorphisms G_i ≅ G_j that are identity on 𝔊 is not unique. It is governed by Z(𝔊)-valued 1-cocycles on γ. This is not discussed here.

ideas.what: Reconstruct an extension G of γ by 𝔊 from a subgroup N_i surjecting onto γ, its intersection SN_i with 𝔊, and a compatible action on 𝔊, via a pushout of extensions
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of a (nonabelian) group extension along a homomorphism of kernels (crossed-module / Baer-type pushout)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Baer; Eilenberg–MacLane nonabelian extension theory; Dedecker for crossed modules)
ideas.where_published: Similar extension yoga appears in SGA 1 Exp. XIII and in the Longue Marche discussion of extensions of Galois groups by fundamental groups

ideas.what: Gluing several such reconstructions by a transitive system of isomorphisms that are identity on 𝔊; encoded as a subgroup of the fibre product ∏_γ G_i meeting 𝔊^I in the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Descent / gluing data for extensions, the fibred-product description of an amalgamation over a common quotient
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche (1981), in the context of reconstructing π_1 from local data; not certain

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine group-theoretic bookkeeping: pushout of extensions and gluing via a fibre product over the common quotient. It is correct and auxiliary to the larger loop-equation programme, with nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: In diagram (15), the top-left entry is N_i (with a struck-out character before it), not 'φN_i'. The square is SN_i → 𝔊, SN_i ⊂ N_i, N_i → G_i (≃ G), 𝔊 ⊂ G_i, with vertical arrows being the inclusions.
The line read 'Une telle donnée implique que on prenne tous la donnée…' is more likely 'Une telle donnée implique en particulier la donnée d'un syst. transitif d'iso entre les γ_i'.
The line 'Identifions maintenant les G_i/𝔊_i = γ_i à γ' should read 'Identifions maintenant les G_i/𝔊 ≃ γ_i à γ'. There is no subscript on 𝔊.
The struck-out heading reads roughly 'Propriétés ... (14), d'où (13)'. It is fully crossed out.
